newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW-Manila bourse head unfazed by scandals.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Manila bourse head unfazed by scandals.

text.p: The president of the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) said on Friday that charges there might be a few bad apples in the country's securities industry did not mean the whole bunch was spoiled.

"Do you know of a stock exchange that is perfect? Even if it's the Tokyo Stock Exchange or the New York Stock Exchange, don't they have problems? Of course, there are," Jose Yulo told Reuters in an interview five days after taking up his post full-time.
"Problems do happen, but that does not necessarily mean that the whole industry is bad," he told Reuters.
A well-known local newspaper columnist recently accused her broker and four securities houses of using her money in unauthorised deals. The four firms have denied any wrongdoing.
She also claimed that some brokers had conspired to manipulate the price of a stock.
The Securities and Exchange Commission and the bourse have launched separate investigations into the columnist's charges. The stock exchange is set to release its findings this month.

Last week, a local newspaper reported that several brokerage houses had violated rules including bans on maintaining dummy accounts and short selling stocks. Yulo said the bourse would look into the report.
Analysts said such reports damaged the credibility of the bourse, which has not yet totally erased its 1970s image of being little more than a house of legalised gambling.
"That's a problem. It's a concern," Yulo said.
He said any expose of wrongdoing should be welcomed since the bourse is trying to purge the industry of unprofessionalism. Broker-members were looking for ways to improve the system, he said.
"There is a persistent, constant effort to operate the exchange as fairly, as transparently and as efficiently as possible. That is a continuing effort."

The exchange has recently come up with several measures to make stock trading more professional by instituting scripless trading and establishing a clearing house. A task force is being created to review trading and disclosure rules.
"The PSE is on its third year. How long does it take for an institution to grow? Maybe five years, 10 years. So it's evolving into that process," he said.
